fields.subnational_unit: Minas Gerais state (municipalities; 2018 cross-section, staffing data 2017)
fields.population: Minas Gerais municipalities reporting to SNIS/IBGE; outliers removed, leaving 574 observations for most variables
fields.sample_size: 574 municipalities after outlier removal for most variables; 391 observations in the final regressions (missing data); plan variable PMSB 456, policy variable PPSB 471 observations
fields.effect_measure: principal-components factor analysis (varimax; four factors, 78.51% variance; KMO 0.675) then three OLS regressions with robust standard errors; factor scores as standardised capacity measures
fields.effect_estimate: Coefficients per factor-score unit (robust SE; p). Water coverage (R2 0.160): financial 6.02 (1.02; <0.001), technical 2.67 (0.99; 0.007), operational 2.41 (0.92; 0.009), POLITICAL (existence of municipal sanitation plan and policy under Law 11,445/2007) -1.89 (0.88; 0.033). Sewerage (R2 0.193): financial 7.36 (1.48; <0.001), technical 3.94 (1.57; 0.013), operational 13.07 (1.65; <0.001), political -0.66 (1.64; 0.687, n.s.). Solid-waste collection (R2 0.567): financial 10.06 (1.41; <0.001), technical 2.25 (1.27; 0.078), operational 28.26 (1.40; <0.001), political +2.56 (1.33; 0.055). Descriptives: 59.8% of municipalities have a plan and 50.9% a policy; plans/policies are less frequent in small municipalities (chi-square, Cramer V medium). The authors explain the negative political coefficient for water as low-coverage municipalities only now planning; they reject only the hypothesis that political capacity affects sewerage.
fields.adjusted_or_unadjusted: adjusted (four capacity factors entered jointly; no demographic or socioeconomic controls beyond the capacity factors)
fields.covariates: four capacity factor scores (financial, technical, operational, political) entered jointly; no GDP, urbanisation or population controls
fields.model_type: principal-components factor analysis followed by OLS with heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors
fields.study_design: cross-sectional municipality-level regression (observational, ecological; one year)
fields.section: Full text (book chapter, Revista/volume on public policies, pp. 441-456): Resumo/Abstract; 3 Procedimentos metodologicos; 4 Resultados e discussao (Tables 2-4); 5 Consideracoes finais

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a municipality-level cross-sectional regression for Minas Gerais (574 municipalities, 391 in the models), read in full text 2026-10-04. Financial, technical and operational capacity are associated with higher water, sewerage and waste-collection coverage; the 'political capacity' factor (having a sanitation plan and policy under Law 11,445/2007) is negative for water (-1.89, p = 0.033), null for sewerage and marginally positive for waste (p = 0.055). Ecological, one year, no controls beyond the capacity factors.
